```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

options(scipen = 999)

lul_d <- read_csv(
  '../data/life-under-lockdown-wave2-extract.csv',
  col_types = cols(
    col_integer(),
    col_factor(),
    col_factor(
      levels = c(
        'Nothing at all',
        'Not very much',
        'A fair amount',
        'A great deal'
      )
    ),
    col_integer()
  )
  )

```

# Hypothesis
H1 Number of unconventional beliefs about coronavirus is associated with gender.

H2 Number of unconventional beliefs about coronavirus is associated with age.

# Descriptive statistics
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = gender
    )
  ) +
  geom_bar()
```

```{r}
lul_d %>%
  count(
    gender
  ) %>%
  kable
```

```{r}
lul_d %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = beliefs)
  ) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 6)
```

```{r}
lul_d %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mdn = median(beliefs),
    M = mean(beliefs),
    SD = sd(beliefs)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```

# Findings
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  group_by(gender) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mdn = median(beliefs),
    M = mean(beliefs),
    SD = sd(beliefs)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r}
lul_d %>%
  filter(gender != 'In another way') %>%
  t.test(
    formula = beliefs ~ gender,
    var.equal = FALSE,
    data = .
  )
```

There were not enough people who identified their gender in another way to include in the analysis. Men had more unconventional beliefs (M = 0.73, SD = 1.13) than women (M = 0.61, SD = 1.05), but this was not statistically significant, t(494.31) = 1.201, p = .230.

```{r}
lul_d %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = age,
      y = beliefs
    )
  ) +
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
lul_d %>%
  cor.test(
    formula = ~ age + beliefs,
    method = 'pearson',
    data = .
  )
```

Age was found to be negatively associated with number of unconventional beliefs, r(498) = -.24, p < .001 95% CI [-.32, -.16].
